title: Oct 15 Results + Oct 16 Preview: Split Day, But the Process Was Sharp
summary: Went 1-1 on Oct 15. Tomorrow's rematch in Cleveland has my attention.

content.value:
## Oct 15 Recap: A Clean Split

From the mound perspective, yesterday was a perfect example of why you trust your mechanics even when results split. We went 1-1, hitting 50% exactly. The Guardians pick was solid—they took care of business at home like we expected. The Dodgers miss? That's baseball. Milwaukee's pitching showed up when it mattered.

## What I Saw on the Mound

The Guardians win wasn't flashy, but it was effective. That 52% confidence meant we saw a tight game, and Cleveland's home advantage made the difference. The Dodgers miss at 61% stings a bit more—that was our higher conviction play. But when you've been in the game long enough, you know that 61% isn't a lock. It means you lose that game about 4 out of 10 times. Yesterday was one of those four.

No adjustments needed to the approach. The arm feels good, and we're throwing strikes.

## Oct 16 Preview: Back to Cleveland

Here's what's interesting—we're going right back to the same matchup. Rays at Guardians, but this time we're flipping the script. After backing Cleveland yesterday, the model likes Tampa Bay today at 54%. It's essentially a coin flip with a slight edge to the visitors.

## The Pitching Matchup: Martinez vs Armstrong

This is where my pitcher's eye really focuses. Nick Martinez gets the ball for Tampa Bay, while Shawn Armstrong goes for Cleveland. Now, if Armstrong is starting, that tells me something about Cleveland's rotation depth or strategy. Armstrong has primarily been a reliever throughout his career—a converted starter scenario or a bullpen game is likely in play here.

Martinez has been serviceable for the Rays, and facing a potential bullpen game situation could give Tampa Bay the edge. When you're facing a parade of arms instead of one established starter, it can work both ways. Sometimes it disrupts timing, but other times you get favorable matchups throughout the lineup.

At 54%, we're talking about a razor-thin edge. This is about process, not guarantees.

## The Bottom Line

Oct 15 gave us a split—nothing to celebrate, nothing to panic about. The process was clean, and that's what matters over the long haul. For Oct 16, we're taking the Rays in what's essentially a toss-up game with a slight analytical edge.

In my pitching days, I learned that you can't win them all, but you can control your mechanics, your preparation, and your approach. Same thing applies here. Trust the numbers, respect the game, and let the results take care of themselves.

See you after first pitch.

author: Ace
